To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the metal-support interface plays a key role in the activation of reactants and the generation of active species in CO oxidation and in the hydrogenation of carbon dioxide; 2) the water-gas-shift reaction occurs on the surface of ceria; 3) the metal-ceria interfaces are the sites of the dissociative adsorption of alcohols, the cleavage of their C-O bonds, and the generation of surface carbon species.

(i) the presence of a metal/ceria interface is crucial to the activation of the reactant molecules; (ii) the presence of metal/ceria interface can also be beneficial in the stabilization of the active phases, thus leading to an increase in catalyst lifetime; (iii) the catalytic activity of the metal particles is enhanced when the metal particles are in intimate contact with ceria.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of model catalysts based on ceria and metal oxides, and the use of these model catalysts to investigate the fundamental properties of metal/cerium oxide interfaces and the catalytic properties of these interfaces in a variety of important reactions, including oxidation, hydrogenation, reforming, and water-gas shift reactions.
the development of new ceria-based catalysts for the production of hydrogen and the selective transformation of hydrocarbons into chemicals and fuels.
the development of new catalytic materials for applications in energy and environmental technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ceria is an excellent support for the preparation of model catalysts and a good promoter for technical catalysts.
the catalytic activity of ceria-metal systems depends not only on the metal but also on the nature of the ceria support and the interface between them.
the metal-ceria interaction is a key factor for the activity of ceria-containing catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal-ceria interfaces are very active in the oxidation reactions and the hydrogenation reactions of CO, CO2 and alcohols.
the metal-ceria interfaces are of great importance in many catalytic reactions and that the use of model catalysts is a very useful approach to study the role of the interface.
the metal-ceria interfaces have been shown to have a crucial role in the activation of C-O bonds and in the formation and stabilization of active phases in the reactions of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal-ceria interaction is a crucial factor for the development of catalytic activity and selectivity in the reactions of interest for the production of hydrogen.
the catalytic properties of metal/ceria systems are strongly dependent on the metal-ceria interaction, which can be tuned by changing the nature of the metal and/or the ceria support.
the catalytic behavior of ceria-based materials is determined by the presence of a metal/ceria interface, where the ceria is in contact with metal nanoparticles, which are the catalytic active sites.
